name: Gale Crater · Mount Sharp Boxwork
story: Two astronauts walk from the habitat up to the boxwork: a web of 1-2 m tall mineral-cemented ridges with sandy hollows between them that Curiosity began exploring in 2025. They sample a ridge and a hollow, visit the rover's track, and walk back before their consumables or daylight run low.

stops.name: Hollow Charlie
tasks: Scoop loose fill from the hollow floor
Trench 10 cm to look for layering
stops.science: Hollows between boxwork ridges are softer bedrock, partly buried by wind-blown sand. Sample the fill and the bedrock beneath it.

stops.name: Ridge Alpha
tasks: Hammer sample of the ridge centre-line
Close-up imaging of the ridge wall
Core drill (5 cm) if footing is safe
stops.science: Boxwork ridges are thought to be fractures filled and hardened by minerals from ancient groundwater, left standing when wind eroded the softer rock around them.

stops.name: Hollow Bravo
stops.science: A second hollow for comparison; Curiosity drove through this part of the boxwork in 2025.

shelters.name: Pressurized rover PR-2
shelters.note: Parked between the hab and the boxwork. Pressurized cabin with a water-wall storm shelter.

skyline_features.name: Aeolis Mons (Mount Sharp) summit
skyline_features.note: about 5.5 km above the crater floor
